title: Prove the sharp Hurwitz budget versus decoding-success law (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof with exact finite corroboration: determine the exact maximum probability that all ten independent uniform b-bit Hurwitz receivers decode correctly under fixed integer copy-charge budget C.

```text
P_max = 2^(-max(0, 5b - floor(C/2)))
```

Saving even one unit below the zero-error floor 10b forces simultaneous failure probability at least 1/2. Successful-fiber counting proves the upper bound; partial mate-parity delivery attains every budget, including the odd-budget plateaus. The proof also covers any abstract matching with the stated tariff and independent random coins under the same per-realization budget.

The contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Alexander Templeton #785 retains the fixed-support nonlinear model and zero-error transcript argument; Douglas R. Colkitt #703 retains the geometry, tariff and transversal method, following Joel Pulikkan #620. Jerry Chen #912 treats a separate adaptive-header expected-cost boundary. These are cited premises; no predecessor result is audited or replayed.

## Evidence

- Before: #785 establishes the zero-error floor and excludes decoding errors.
- After: an all-width written sharp tradeoff, a matching code, and a new exact finite decoder census.
- All 65,536 Boolean one-bit broadcasts on two mate pairs receive exact decoder optimization by conflict-graph independent sets, then literal optimal decoding on 1,048,576 input tuples. The optimal-success histogram, counted over encoders, is `4:1810, 5:17632, 6:28256, 7:15136, 8:2702` out of 16 inputs.
- 117 partial-parity code cases pass over 143,235 literal input tuples. Five invalid cases reject; odd-budget rounding, omitted parity, correlated-input boundaries and conflicting decodes are distinguished.
- Both registered warning-strict checks pass locally on CPython 3.12.15: normal 0.822 seconds, optimized 0.793 seconds. These are replay-duration measurements for the CI limit, not performance comparisons.
- Metadata replay, seven-file committed-byte/source-history preflight, official committed export integrity, Git-free normal/optimized replay, and proof/receipt corruption controls pass. Every exported byte is restored. Local replay planning selects only this package.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/hurwitz-budget-success/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/hurwitz-budget-success/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/hurwitz-budget-success
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/hurwitz-budget-success --check-source-history
```

The direct marker is `PASS_HURWITZ_BUDGET_SUCCESS`. The generated receipt binds the proof, verifier and metadata hashes. On another machine, substitute its CPython 3.12 executable for the absolute interpreter path.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

Fixed source/reader supports and widths, independent uniform inputs, mate-only free side information and additive pairing-rank pricing remain premises. The result measures simultaneous correctness, not marginal errors. It does not cover an expected-charge budget, adaptive/private routing, variable lengths or interactive relays. Physical encoding, decoding, source access, hosting, cleanup and tape costs are unknown. No physical supplier, new kappa, selected-frontier change or complete multiplication theorem is claimed. No native/Lean/full-selected replay or independent human/formal-kernel proof review was run.

## Open next questions

- Determine the achievable individual-receiver error vectors, starting with two mate pairs and one broadcast bit.
- Determine the sharp unequal-width counterpart, starting with two mate pairs of widths (1,2,1,1). Transversal dimensions then differ.

## Related open work

No other open PR studying this Hurwitz budget/simultaneous-success quantity was found in the refreshed titles/body search. #703, #785 and #912 are merged predecessors. Concurrent Gaussian localized-header work concerns a different geometry and a zero-error expected-cost question.
